content.text:
I submitted **index 89** (Fe 0.26, Ni 0.17, V 0.56), which gave the highest photocurrent of the three samples I measured: **3.24 µA**. That's the best of my three measurements. I can't tell how close it is to the library's best, because 157 compositions went unmeasured.

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 158 | 0.53 / 0.18 / 0.29 | 1.72 µA |
| 34 | 0.39 / 0.18 / 0.42 | 2.80 µA |
| 89 | 0.26 / 0.17 / 0.56 | 3.24 µA |

- **Why these three:** the models favoured an Fe–V oxide with little Ni.
  - FeVO4 is stable in the MACE model, with a predicted band gap of 2.75 eV. That is small enough to absorb the 3.2 eV light.
  - V2O5's predicted gap is 2.83 eV, so it absorbs too.
  - A made-up Ni version of FeVO4 came out with a gap of only about 0.5 eV, so I kept Ni low.
- **Trend:** at similar low Ni, photocurrent rose as V went up and Fe went down, and I followed that toward the V-rich side.
- **Budget:** all 3 photocurrent measurements are used. I skipped XRD (5 scans unused), so the phases on the film are inferred from the models, not confirmed.

The trend was still rising at index 89, so more V-rich, low-Ni samples such as index 13 or 77 might do better. I couldn't test that with the budget spent.
